newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki bourse, derivatives exchange SOM to merge.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki bourse, derivatives exchange SOM to merge.

text.p: The Helsinki Stock Exchange and Finnish derivatives exchange SOM Oy said in a joint statement on Tuesday they would merge with the aim of enhancing Finnish capital markets by simplifying their structure.
"The name of the new company will be HEX Oy, Helsingin Arvopaperi- ja johdannaisporssi, selvitysyhtio," they said.

If all current owners convert shares, banking group Merita will be the largest owner of the new exchange with a 29.8 percent stake, and Swedish OM Gruppen will be the second largest with a 15.7 percent holding, they said.

"According to the merger agreement, shares in Helsinki Stock Exchange will be converted into shares in the new company on a 100:122 basis and shares of SOM on a 100:597 basis," they said, adding the share capital would be about 100 million markka.

"If all existing shareholders become shareholders also in the new company the five major shareholders will be Merita Group (29.8 percent), OM Gruppen AB (15.7 percent), OKOBANK (6.7 percent), Postipankki Ltd (6.4 percent) and Evli Group (4.8 percent)," the statement said, adding that voting power was limited to 1/20 of the total votes.
The total holdings of other issuers will be 19.9 percent and those of other brokerage houses 17.5 percent, it added.

The new company's full name in English will be HEX Ltd, Helsinki Stock and Derivatives Exchange, Clearing House, and it will be the parent company of two subsidiaries -- the El-Ex electricity exchange, and Somtel Ltd, they said.

Bourse CEO Juhani Erma will become president and chief executive officer of HEX Ltd and Asko Schrey, Managing Director of SOM will be appointed chief operating officer and deputy chief executive officer, it said.
Last year, the combined turnover of the merging companies was 97 million markka and the profits 34 million markka.

"The merger will promote international cooperation based on networking and provide the Finnish investors with tools for improved risk diversification," they said. "Furthermore, it will open new possibilities for product development."

"Networking and open interface applications of the company's information systems will provide a good basis for a versatile service range aimed at market participants," it said, noting both cash and derivatives services will be available from one organisation.
The exchanges said SOM's products can be traded in Stockholm and at the market operated by OM's London-based exchange, OMLX and that, correspondingly, the products of OM can be traded in Finland.
"The agreement also includes some forms of cooperation on the equity market," they added.

"Furthermore, the merger will indirectly strengthen and expand the ownership structure of EL-EX Electricity Exchange and its qualifications for operating on the Nordic electricity market," they added.
